payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones

program.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
requirements.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones

outcomes.description: Move the mug so that it is positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.target: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.reference: The headphones in the image; compare the mug’s position with the headphones.

nodes.question: Does comparison of the source and edited images establish that the source mug itself has been moved to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when the combined visual evidence establishes both correspondence to the source mug and its position to the right of the edited headphones. Compare both edited mug candidates using body proportions, rim and interior, handle geometry, relative scale and appearance, accounting for changes in framing and possible rotation. Generic mug shape, similar taper or presence on the right is insufficient when those cues do not distinguish the right-hand candidate from the left-hand candidate. Consider evidence supporting and contradicting each correspondence; do not dismiss differences in interior, handle or appearance without weighing them together with the supporting cues. Exact color, scale and handle orientation preservation are not separate requirements. Fail when the evidence establishes that the source mug remains left of the headphones or otherwise has not reached the requested right-side position. Use unknown when the source mug's correspondence or resulting position remains unresolved. A blurred patch alone establishes neither retained identity nor successful removal, and lack of proof of completion is not proof of failure.
nodes.binding: Target: the light-blue mug with a left-facing handle in the source image. Reference: the headphones in each image. Compare the source mug with both edited candidates: the pale mug left of the headphones and the dark-interior mug right of the headphones. Inspect the far-left blue blurred patch only as ambiguous possible residual evidence, not as an identified mug. Assess whether the full cue combination distinguishes the right-hand candidate as the relocated source mug rather than a separate mug; if neither candidate can be identified reliably, return unknown. Compare object-relative placement with the edited headphones, allowing for changed framing, scale and headphone arrangement rather than relying on raw pixel coordinates.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d1: The binding is already specific; the unresolved result is not a schema, transport, or dependency failure (the check ran validly with no dependencies). Improve the decision criterion’s evidence integration rather than forcing the reference label: compare the source mug’s broad body and dark-blue interior with both edited candidates, and weigh the right candidate’s dark interior as a meaningful identity cue alongside its smaller/tapered body and right-facing handle. The pale left candidate’s light interior and different appearance also count against it. Do not treat changed scale, color, or handle orientation as automatic disproof, since these are not required invariants; likewise, do not infer identity from right-side placement alone. The far-left blur remains ambiguous and cannot establish either a retained mug or successful removal. The trace’s high confidence despite unresolved correspondence is a calibration signal: make confidence reflect the strength and conflict of the combined cues, and distinguish uncertainty about identity from evidence that some requested movement may have progressed. Keep unknown when correspondence truly cannot be resolved; do not convert the aggregate ‘partial’ label into atomic ground truth or lower the pass/fail standard merely to match it.

observations.evidence: The source mug is light blue, relatively broad, with a left-facing handle and a dark blue interior. In the edited image, the pale mug left of the headphones has a right-facing handle and light interior, while the dark-interior mug to the right has a right-facing handle and appears smaller and more tapered. The right-hand candidate's dark interior is a supporting cue, but its appearance, proportions, scale, and handle orientation differ; the left candidate also differs in color, interior, and handle orientation. The far-left blue blur is ambiguous and does not establish identity. The visual evidence does not reliably distinguish which edited mug, if either, is the source mug, so its resulting position is unresolved.

findings.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
findings.question: Does the edited image provide evidence that the source mug was removed from its original left-of-headphones position, independently of whether either visible mug can be identified as the relocated mug?
findings.criteria: Inspect the source mug’s former location and the far-left blue blurred patch in the edited image. Determine whether the patch is merely a lighting/reflection artifact or contains residual mug structure (such as a rim, body boundary, or handle). Do not treat blur or absence of a clearly recognizable mug as proof of removal; report unknown if the evidence cannot distinguish these possibilities.
findings.evidence: The source shows a distinct light-blue mug left of the headphones. The edited image has a blue blurred patch at the far left, but no clearly discernible rim or handle; the two visible mugs are elsewhere.
findings.rationale: The existing check notes the patch as ambiguous but does not separately investigate whether the source mug remains at its original location. That evidence could help judge whether the requested move progressed, while not resolving which visible mug, if either, is the source mug.

decisions.question: Does comparison of the source and edited images establish that the source mug has been relocated to the right of the headphones?
decisions.criteria: Pass when the combined visual evidence sufficiently supports correspondence between the source mug and an edited mug positioned to the right of the edited headphones. Compare both edited candidates explicitly: the source mug has a broad light-blue body, blue interior with a dark lower region, and a left-facing handle; the right candidate has a dark interior, smaller and more tapered body, and right-facing handle; the left candidate has a light interior and different appearance. Weigh interior appearance as a meaningful comparative cue together with body proportions, rim, handle geometry, surface appearance and relative scale. Account for the substantially changed framing, lighting and possible rotation; differences in color, scale or handle orientation are not automatic disproof or independent failures. Neither dark interior alone nor right-side placement alone establishes identity. Explain why the full cue combination supports one candidate over the other, or why it remains inconclusive. Inspect the former mug location for recognizable residual structure, but do not infer retention or successful removal from the far-left blue blur alone. Fail only when the evidence establishes that the source mug remains left of the headphones or otherwise has not reached the requested right-side position. Return unknown when correspondence or resulting placement cannot be established; absence of proof of completion is not proof of failure. Calibrate confidence to the strength and conflict of the visual evidence rather than reporting strong confidence in an unresolved identity judgment.
decisions.binding: Target: the light-blue mug with a left-facing handle in the source image. Reference: the headphones in each image. Compare the source mug with both edited candidates: the pale mug left of the headphones and the dark-interior mug right of the headphones. Inspect the far-left blue blurred patch only as ambiguous possible residual evidence, not as an identified mug. Assess which candidate, if either, corresponds to the relocated source mug using the combined visual cues. Compare object-relative placement with the edited headphones, allowing for changed framing, scale and headphone arrangement rather than relying on raw pixel coordinates.
